question: The World Medical Association's Declaration of Geneva that is currently operative for Indian medical graduates was last revised in which year?

answers.text: 1948 — the original version adopted at the WMA General Assembly in Geneva

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 1948 was the year of the original Declaration. The document has been revised multiple times since, with the most recent and operative revision in 2017.

answers.text: 1983 — the version that added the 'Health of my patient will be my first consideration' clause

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 1983 was one of several revisions, but it is not the current operative version. The 2017 revision added new commitments, including on physician wellbeing and non-discrimination.

answers.text: 2017 — the most recent WMA revision, which is the version currently in force

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 2017 WMA revision is the current operative Declaration of Geneva. It added new commitments including the physician's own health and wellbeing, and strengthened non-discrimination language.

answers.text: 2022 — a post-pandemic revision responding to COVID-19 and global health emergencies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. There was no 2022 revision. The most recent revision is 2017.

overallFeedback.feedback: The Declaration of Geneva was last revised in 2017 by the WMA. This is the current operative version and the one relevant to Indian medical graduation.
Correct. The 2017 WMA revision is the operative Declaration of Geneva. It is this version that underlies the oath administered at Indian medical graduation ceremonies.
